description: I’m an independent game developer based in Japan. For this challenge, I built Paper Earth, a small web prototype that lets visitors compare NASA Terra MODIS land surface temperature maps around Kyoto Station on two dates. I’m working solo on this project.
summary:
Paper Earth is a web prototype for comparing daytime land surface temperature around Kyoto Station, Japan. Visitors can switch between NASA Terra MODIS maps from August 18 and December 18, 2025, and compare the same area on a shared temperature scale. Missing observations are left blank.

The prototype addresses the visualization part of the Earth System Trend Detective challenge. It gives students and curious visitors a way to explore how surface temperatures differed across Kyoto on two selected days. A longer time series would be needed to estimate a trend or test its statistical significance.
details:
I built a browser-based comparison of two daytime land surface temperature maps around Kyoto Station. The date buttons switch between August 18 and December 18, 2025. Both maps use the same geographic extent and color scale, with a marker for Kyoto Station to help visitors orient themselves.

The maps come from NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS), using the MODIS_Terra_Land_Surface_Temp_Day layer. The underlying dataset is Terra MODIS MOD11A1 Version 6.1, with a native resolution of approximately 1 km. I used the rendered NASA imagery, overlaid the station marker, and left missing pixels blank. The temperatures describe the land surface. The resolution is too coarse to interpret individual buildings, and values read from the color legend are approximate. The two dates show a snapshot comparison. No long-term trend or statistical significance was calculated.

I built the comparison page and its three-slide demo during the hackathon using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and hosted them on Cloudflare Pages. My earlier PaperPLATEAU project inspired the idea of exploring a familiar place. This submission uses its own code and NASA imagery.

AI disclosure: Claude Code helped retrieve imagery, write the webpage and demo code, deploy the site, and check links. Claude Code and ChatGPT helped draft and revise the English submission text. The satellite maps are NASA GIBS imagery.
